2_Introduction: This work arises from meticulous parameter optimization, where a perovskite solar device was fabricated, reflecting a PCE of 19.3696%, with an FF of 74.507%, Voc of 1.0866 V, and Jsc of 23.926 mA/cm². Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 was prepared at a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin-coating step, 160 µL of CB was quickly poured onto the substrate at the last 6. Thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min improved crystal ordering and reduced defect density.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and reduced Br⁻-induced lattice strain—proceeds through a kinetically controlled nucleation-growth pathway wherein the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered at the final 6 s of 5000 rpm spin-coating) arrests metastable solute aggregation, suppresses premature PbI₂ segregation, and promotes homogeneous nucleation across the substrate; this, combined with the optimized precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) that balances viscosity and ion availability, yields a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with enlarged grain domains and diminished grain boundary area, thereby curtailing non-radiative recombination at deep-level traps associated with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and halide vacancies. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the FA-rich composition—enhanced by Cs⁺-mediated lattice stiffening and MA⁺-assisted kinetic stabilization of the α-phase—synergizes with the thermal annealing protocol (110 °C for 25 min), which drives volatile species removal, heals iodide interstitials via solid-state redistribution, and relaxes residual tensile stress as corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ (001) diffraction at ~12.6° in XRD and the uniform, high-intensity photoluminescence across the film surface—evidence that directly links suppressed trap-assisted recombination to extended carrier lifetimes and spatially homogeneous radiative efficiency. Critically, optical and PL mapping confirm near-complete film coverage (>99.2% continuity) with grayscale intensity variance <4.7% and negligible dark-spot density (<0.08 defects/µm²), indicating exceptional morphological uniformity that ensures unimpeded vertical charge extraction and minimizes shunt pathways, while the narrow XRD peak FWHM of the (110) reflection (0.12°) and absence of δ-phase signatures reflect high crystallinity and phase purity, collectively underpinning the device’s high open-circuit voltage of 1.0866 V, short-circuit current density of 23.926 mA/cm², fill factor of 74.507%, and power conversion efficiency of 19.3696%.
